- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in early days of the 30-day horizon.
- Forecasts tend to be too low in the first 5–10 days, then gradually rise — suggesting a lag in capturing short-term momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 60+), model overreacts with overshoots in the immediate following days.
- Model shows weak mean reversion — fails to pull prices back toward historical averages after peaks.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day window, underestimating true values.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the middle of the forecast horizon (days 15–25), often missing upward trends.
- Forecasts are too smooth — fail to capture volatility clustering or sudden reversals in price direction.
- Model tends to underestimate the true price at the end of the forecast window (last 5–10 days), suggesting horizon-specific bias.
